stories.headline: Tidal to ban AI-generated music from December 9
stories.summary: Tidal will stop accepting fully AI-generated music on December 9 and will remove about 29 million such songs. It expects to reject roughly 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day, and still allows tracks made with AI assistance.
stories.why: Streaming platforms are tightening content rules for AI output, which affects any team building generative audio, upload, or moderation pipelines.

sources.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming

stories.headline: Anthropic shares slip below IPO price
stories.summary: Anthropic's stock has fallen under its IPO price since listing. Coverage says the slump could pressure valuations across AI startups.
stories.why: A weak debut for a leading AI lab may make investors more cautious about funding and valuing AI companies, which shapes hiring and runway for software teams.

sources.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups

stories.headline: Amazon reportedly buys Decart for $7.5 billion
stories.summary: Amazon is reported to be acquiring Decart for about $7.5 billion. The deal is part of a push to improve the efficiency of its Trainium chips and reduce its reliance on Nvidia hardware through software.
stories.why: Big cloud providers investing in custom-chip software signals a shift in the tooling and performance options available to teams training and serving models.

sources.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia

stories.headline: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia amid affair reports and scrutiny
stories.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has returned as CEO after a leave tied to reports of affairs. At his first all-hands he apologised to staff and denied that the White House helped secure his return. Commentators question the board's exposure and Nvidia's role in US industry.
stories.why: Leadership turmoil at the dominant AI chip supplier could affect supply, roadmap stability, and the wider market for AI infrastructure.

sources.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?

stories.headline: UK cyber agency warns AI attacks exploit basic security gaps
stories.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre says AI-driven hacking tools mainly exploit simple, long-standing security flaws. It argues that organisations need stronger foundations.
stories.why: Engineering leaders should treat basic hygiene such as patching and access control as the first defence against AI-assisted attacks.

sources.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security

stories.headline: New benchmark finds AI agents unreliable at everyday tasks
stories.summary: A new benchmark shows that leading AI models still struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely, and can introduce new problems while doing them.
stories.why: It is a reminder that agent products need strong evaluation, guardrails, and error handling before they are trusted with real user workflows.

sources.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life

stories.headline: Active intrusion campaign targets Check Point security management servers
stories.summary: An ongoing intrusion campaign is reported to be targeting Check Point security management servers. The report drew significant discussion on Hacker News.
stories.why: Teams that run or depend on these management servers should check their exposure and monitor for compromise.

sources.title: Active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers

stories.headline: Rust 1.100 stabilises the never type after a decade of work
stories.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released 12 November, stabilises the never type (!) and makes Infallible an alias for it. It also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and adds an opt-in dependency cooldown setting to Cargo.
stories.why: The dependency cooldown option gives teams a new way to limit how quickly they pick up fresh package versions.

sources.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts

stories.headline: AWS doubles Lambda maximum timeout to 30 minutes
stories.summary: AWS has raised the maximum timeout for on-demand Lambda event functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions. No opt-in is required and there is no new pricing, and AWS lists the related effects on concurrency and SQS and Kafka settings.
stories.why: Longer timeouts let teams run longer jobs in Lambda, but AWS's notes on concurrency and event-source settings mean architectures should be reviewed.

sources.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15

stories.headline: OpenAI details Pando, a Git backend built for coding agents
stories.summary: OpenAI has described Pando, a backend that scales Git for many concurrent coding-agent workloads while keeping standard Git workflows. The company reports a nearly 80% reduction in median push latency.
stories.why: As agents push code in parallel, Git hosting infrastructure may need to scale in similar ways.

sources.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando

stories.headline: CNCF research finds virtual machines still host most production workloads
stories.summary: New CNCF and Linux Foundation Research data shows VMs host an average of 53% of production applications. Demand for VMs is also rising from AI and agentic workloads that need stronger execution isolation.
stories.why: Platform teams planning AI infrastructure should expect VMs to remain a core part of production hosting.

sources.title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve

stories.headline: Microsoft declares 'Code Red' after near-24-hour Outlook and Exchange outage
stories.summary: A nearly 24-hour Exchange Online and Outlook outage cut off email for millions of customers. Microsoft traced it to a bug that had sat on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers, and it has declared an unusual internal 'Code Red'.
stories.why: Shows how a latent bug in shared networking infrastructure can take down a major service, and why recovery-time targets are now under scrutiny.

sources.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage
Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”

stories.headline: Amazon says attackers' AI agents found and exploited a zero-day with little human input
stories.summary: Amazon reports that hackers used AI agents to discover and exploit a zero-day vulnerability with minimal human direction. The company describes the Cairn AI framework as useful to both attackers and defenders.
stories.why: Autonomous AI tooling is shortening the time from vulnerability discovery to exploitation, which changes how teams should prioritise patching.

sources.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

stories.headline: Dozens of oil and chemical shipping vessels hit by cyberattacks, Iran suspected
stories.summary: A report says dozens of oil and chemical tankers have been hacked in recent weeks. Iran is named as the main suspect behind the campaign.
stories.why: Operational technology on ships is a growing target, and the attacks highlight risks for any industrial system with weak remote access controls.

sources.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report

stories.headline: US financial crimes bureau FinCEN investigating unauthorised access to its systems
stories.summary: FinCEN, part of the Treasury Department, disclosed a cybersecurity incident that gave unauthorised access to a limited subset of its systems. It has not yet shared further details.
stories.why: A government agency confirming intrusion into its systems is a reminder that access controls and audit logging matter for any sensitive data store.

sources.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’

stories.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets
stories.summary: A federal jury in New York has convicted Huawei of stealing trade secrets from US companies. The case alleged theft of source code and proprietary technology from several firms.
stories.why: The verdict brings a long-running trade secrets case to a close and may affect how companies handle source code and vendor relationships with Chinese firms.

sources.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets

stories.headline: Claude-BugHunter, a Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting, trends on GitHub
stories.summary: The Python repo, which packages 84 skills and 15 slash commands for vulnerability research and external red-team work, gained about 1,800 stars in a day. It is a community project, and its claimed coverage of disclosed-report patterns has not been independently verified.
stories.why: Security-focused agent skills are spreading fast, so teams should weigh how they use AI tools for offensive testing and what that means for their review process.

sources.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 84 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerabilit

stories.headline: CLI-Anything aims to make all software usable by AI agents through a CLI hub
stories.summary: The Python project, titled 'Making ALL Software Agent-Native', added about 1,070 stars today and has over 65,000 in total. It pitches a shared command-line hub so agents can drive existing tools, which is a broad ambition still to be proven.
stories.why: If agents can reliably operate ordinary CLIs, the interfaces teams build and maintain will matter more for automation than they do now.

sources.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

stories.headline: Superpowers, an agentic skills framework for software development, keeps climbing
stories.summary: The Shell project, which describes itself as a methodology for software development with agents, gained about 1,000 stars today and now has more than 326,000. Its popularity signals strong interest, though it is a community framework rather than a proven standard.
stories.why: Shared methodologies for agents shape how teams structure coding workflows, so leaders may want to evaluate them before ad hoc prompting spreads.

sources.title: obra/superpowers: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

stories.headline: Firecrawl pitches a single API for agent search, scraping and data access
stories.summary: The TypeScript project offers search, scraping and access to more than 550 data providers through one API for agents. It gained about 990 stars today, reaching roughly 209,000 in total.
stories.why: Data access for agents is becoming a build-or-buy decision, and a unified API could reduce the custom scraping and integration work teams maintain.

sources.title: firecrawl/firecrawl: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

stories.headline: Cursor publishes a plugin specification and official plugins on GitHub
stories.summary: Cursor has released a plugin specification and a set of official plugins in a public repository, which is trending with about 360 stars today. The release defines how third parties can extend the editor, though adoption is still early.
stories.why: A public plugin spec from a major AI coding editor could set a pattern for extending developer tools, which matters to teams that customise their IDE workflows.

sources.title: cursor/plugins: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins

stories.headline: JetBrains CEO gives manual code review two years
stories.summary: JetBrains' CEO predicts that manual code review may be ending within about two years. LeadDev raised the question in a feature on the future of code review.
stories.why: If AI tools take over review work, teams will need new norms for quality checks and accountability for shipped code.

sources.title: The end of manual code review?

stories.headline: Less experienced developers trust AI more, eroding code ownership
stories.summary: A LeadDev article reports that less experienced developers tend to trust AI-generated code more, which it says is weakening code ownership.
stories.why: Leaders need to make sure engineers still understand and take responsibility for code that AI helped write.

sources.title: Code ownership is eroding

stories.headline: Capital One treats multi-agent AI as a platform problem
stories.summary: A LeadDev feature looks at how Capital One runs its multi-agent AI system, framing the work as a platform challenge rather than a set of separate tools.
stories.why: It shows how a large bank organises shared infrastructure for AI agents, a question many engineering leaders now face.

sources.title: Inside Capital One’s multi-agent system

stories.headline: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, with the gap widening with age
stories.summary: An analysis of 149 studies found cannabis users developed psychosis about 2.5 years earlier than non-users on average. The gap grew to over six years among adults aged 30 and older.
stories.why: Teams building health or wellbeing products should note that cannabis-related psychiatric risk may build up over time, not just appear early on.

sources.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

stories.headline: Researchers identify a 'circadian depression' subtype linked to the body clock
stories.summary: Researchers describe a depression subtype tied to the body's internal clock, linked to night-owl habits, excessive sleep and persistent exhaustion. It may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, and common antidepressants often struggle to treat it.
stories.why: Sleep timing may become a useful marker for matching people with treatments, which matters for anyone building mental health tools.

sources.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

stories.headline: AI may not process information the way the human brain does
stories.summary: Researchers report that AI models which closely predict brain activity may still rely on internal processes the brain does not use. The finding challenges how scientists read the link between artificial and biological intelligence.
stories.why: Engineers who lean on brain analogies to explain or design AI systems may be relying on comparisons that do not hold.

sources.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover

stories.headline: AI analysis of children's brain scans finds three brain types behind ADHD and anxiety
stories.summary: An AI-driven analysis of thousands of children's brain scans identified three biological patterns that cut across traditional ADHD and anxiety diagnoses. The patterns can appear before a diagnosis is made, which could allow earlier and more personalised care.
stories.why: It shows how machine learning on large imaging datasets is being used to reframe clinical categories, a pattern relevant to health-tech builders.

sources.title: Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety

stories.headline: Dell's AI server demand more than doubles sales; $25B buyback authorised
stories.summary: Dell reported third-quarter overall sales that more than doubled year on year, driven by AI server demand, and authorised a $25 billion share buyback. Its stock rose after the results.
stories.why: Sustained AI server demand signals continued heavy infrastructure spending that engineering teams will feel in hardware availability and cloud pricing.

sources.title: Dell’s stock rises as the AI boom helps sales more than double
Dell earnings beat on AI strength, company authorizes $25 billion buyback

stories.headline: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed in pharma's biggest deal in three years
stories.summary: Sanofi has agreed to acquire drugmaker Insmed, and Insmed's shares rose 14% on the news. Sanofi faces falling revenue later this decade as its top-selling drugs lose exclusivity.
stories.why: Patent expiries pushing pharma toward large acquisitions can reshape which research and data platforms life-sciences firms invest in.

sources.title: Drugmaker Insmed shares rally 14% after Sanofi agrees to buy it in pharma’s biggest deal in three years

stories.headline: Xiamen Airlines to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 jets in a deal worth about $7.4B
stories.summary: China's Xiamen Airlines has agreed to purchase 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft, with a combined catalogue price of around $7.4 billion.
stories.why: Large aircraft orders keep aerospace manufacturing and its supplier software and systems ecosystem busy for years.

sources.title: China’s Xiamen Airlines to buy 50 Boeing jets in $7.4 billion deal

stories.headline: Meta's Muse AI agent carries no ads but lifts its ad business via Instagram
stories.summary: Meta says its Muse personal AI agent does not show ads, yet the tool is already boosting the company's advertising business, according to a senior executive speaking to CNBC.
stories.why: It shows how AI assistants can drive revenue for existing products, a pattern product teams weigh when planning monetisation.

sources.title: How Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent
